To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a method to culture sponge-associated bacteria based on sponge physiological and genomic data, and have used this approach to isolate new sponge-associated bacterial species.
we developed new culture media and culture conditions that led to the isolation and cultivation of bacteria that are associated with the Red Sea sponge T. swinhoei.

we used sponge-associated bacteria physiological and genomic information, in combination with diverse culture media and culture conditions, to enhance the culturable bacterial diversity of Theonella swinhoi.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of genomic and physiological information to enhance the isolation of sponge-associated bacteria and their culturable diversity.
the use of sponge physiology to improve culturing of its associated bacteria.
the development of novel culture conditions for the isolation of bacteria from marine sponges.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of a combination of sponge physiological and genomic data to reflect the environment in which the sponge-associated bacteria live, along with the application of novel culturing conditions, led to a higher diversity of culturable sponge-associated bacteria.

the combined use of physiological and genomic information of the host, along with the use of a variety of culture media, and different growth conditions, can be an efficient way to enhance the diversity and the culturability of the bacteria associated with sponges.
the sponge microbiome has been underestimated and that its culturable fraction is still largely unknown.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sponge-associated bacteria can be cultivated in the laboratory using a combination of genomic and physiological data of the sponge and its symbionts.
sponge-associated bacteria are diverse, and the use of sponge physiology and genomic information can be a powerful tool to enhance the diversity and number of cultured bacteria.

we were able to isolate bacteria from a sponge using a combination of sponge physiological data and sponge genomic data, and that the use of such data led to an increase in diversity of sponge-associated bacteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sponge-associated bacterial diversity can be enhanced using sponge-specific culturing conditions.
sponge-associated bacteria, like other marine bacteria, can be cultivated using a variety of media and conditions.
the sponge-associated microbiome can be enriched and the diversity of culturable bacteria can be increased using sponge-specific physiological information.
